claims.years: Compilation as on 11 November 2025; historical versions not reconstructed
claims.procedure: Population-proportional SC/ST quotas and women’s minimum shares; territorial allotment may rotate.
claims.paraphrase: Seat quotas are distinguished from chairperson-office reservation.
claims.qualification: Not a rule specifying a unique lottery algorithm.
claims.evidence_basis: Official Legislative Department PDF.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Compare like offices and eligible pools.
claims.contradiction: An allocation below an applicable constitutional minimum, after verifying denominators and legally applicable exceptions, would contradict compliant implementation; the provision alone supplies no unique lottery test.
claims.required_inputs: Election-specific implementing law and constituency populations.

claims.quote: in such manner as the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide
claims.years: Compilation as on 11 November 2025; historical versions not reconstructed
claims.procedure: State-law implementation; constitutional minimum shares and rotation of reserved offices.
claims.paraphrase: The Constitution delegates the manner of chairperson reservation to State law.
claims.qualification: Delegation to States does not authorize district-specific departures from State rules.
claims.evidence_basis: Official Legislative Department PDF.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Geographic residuals alone cannot establish lawful discretion.
claims.contradiction: An allocation violating applicable chairperson minima or the prescribed rotation would contradict compliant implementation after historical law and eligible offices are established; geographic heterogeneity alone would not.
claims.required_inputs: Applicable State enactments, amendments and election orders.

claims.printed_page: No printed page number on inspected pages
claims.pool: Offices at each level in the State
claims.procedure: Population-proportional SC/ST offices; women’s minimum; rotation in prescribed manner.
claims.paraphrase: The Act requires rotation of reserved chairperson offices but leaves its implementation to prescription.
claims.qualification: The inspected compilation is not a verified statement of the women’s quota for every observed election.
claims.evidence_basis: Official Ministry download, directly inspected via PDF extraction.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Rotation does not itself specify a probability model.
claims.contradiction: Failure to rotate as required by the applicable implementing prescription would contradict compliant implementation; the Act alone does not imply a unique one-cycle transition matrix.
claims.required_inputs: Amendment chronology and election-specific implementing rules.

claims.pool: Panchayat Samiti / Zila Parishad as specified
claims.procedure: Authorized officer determines reserved numbers; Rule 9(2) refers SC/ST/backward-class allocation to Rule 7.
claims.paraphrase: An authorized officer determines reserved numbers; Rule 9(2) refers SC/ST/backward-class allocation to Rule 7.
claims.qualification: Rule 9(2) does not name women in its Rule 7 cross-reference.
claims.evidence_basis: Official India Code indexed source text; full PDF unavailable.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Authorized implementation is not evidence of unconstrained discretion.
claims.contradiction: A documented allocation made without the required authorization or contrary to the applicable cross-referenced procedure would contradict compliant implementation; residual geographic variation alone would not.
claims.required_inputs: Historical gazettes, officer orders and allocation records.

claims.pool: Offices in the district; operational strata require confirmation
claims.procedure: Authorized officer determines reserved women’s offices by lot.
claims.paraphrase: The rule expressly specifies a lottery for women’s chairperson offices.
claims.qualification: A lottery prescription alone does not identify eligibility exclusions or independence across cycles.
claims.evidence_basis: Official India Code indexed source text; full PDF unavailable.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Test lottery benchmarks only after reconstructing eligible pools.
claims.contradiction: A documented deterministic selection replacing the required draw, or repeated statistically calibrated departures from the reconstructed lottery distribution, would count against implementation of the prescribed lottery.
claims.required_inputs: Contemporaneous rules, lottery registers, pools, caste strata and boundary histories.

claims.pool: Previously allotted wards/constituencies within the rotation cycle
claims.procedure: Prior lot-selected units excluded from subsequent draws until completion of cycle.
claims.paraphrase: The quoted nonrepeat provision expressly concerns wards and constituencies.
claims.qualification: Do not automatically transfer this provision to Sarpanch offices under Rule 9.
claims.evidence_basis: Official India Code indexed source text; full PDF unavailable.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: Consecutive women’s head reservation is not by itself a verified violation of Rule 7(13).
claims.contradiction: Re-selection of an otherwise excluded ward or constituency before completion of its applicable rotation cycle would contradict the stated exclusion; a repeated Sarpanch reservation alone would not.
claims.required_inputs: Applicable legal interpretation and office-specific historical orders.

claims.quote: shall be allotted by rotation to different Gram Panchayats
claims.procedure: State-order reservation; proportional caste shares, backward-class ceiling, women’s minima and prescribed rotation.
claims.paraphrase: The Act requires rotation in a separately prescribed order.
claims.qualification: This passage does not specify the ranking variable, tie rule or reset year.
claims.evidence_basis: Official Ministry PDF directly inspected.
claims.cited_origin: Primary legal provision identified in the section field; historical applicability remains subject to the stated qualification.
claims.implication: A population-rank reconstruction needs subordinate rules.
claims.contradiction: An office allocation contrary to the historically applicable prescribed order would contradict compliant implementation; no unique falsification is implied until that subordinate prescription is recovered.
claims.required_inputs: Election-specific reservation rules and orders.

claims.quote: rank GPs according to their proportion of SCs
claims.procedure: Descending SC share; successive elections move down the list.
claims.paraphrase: The account assigns SC offices using a rotating population-share ranking.
claims.qualification: The 64-GP survey sample is distinct from the 570-GP reconstruction reported in Online Appendix B.
claims.evidence_basis: Main-text account and Jalore rotation table; Online Appendix B separately checks observed versus predicted timing across 16 Samitis.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Reconstruct ranks and histories before evaluating deviations.
claims.contradiction: An eligible GP below the reconstructed SC-share cutoff being selected while an otherwise eligible higher-ranked GP remains open would contradict the stated deterministic ranking, after resolving ties and prior-cycle exclusions.
claims.required_inputs: Historical GP composition, Census counts, reservation history and pool quotas.

claims.pool: Previously unreserved GPs near Samiti cutoffs
claims.procedure: Matched pairs around the reservation threshold.
claims.paraphrase: The design compares newly reserved GPs with nearby unreserved ranks.
claims.qualification: Appendix B, p. 10, reports that no survey GP meets the author’s suspicious-misassignment definition; it does not report zero discrepancies of every kind among survey GPs.
claims.evidence_basis: Main-text sampling account, Table 1 and Online Appendix B, pp. 9–10.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Audit full pools and report deviations beyond selected pairs.
claims.contradiction: Sampled treated and comparison GPs lying on the same side of the correctly reconstructed cutoff, or not meeting the stated prior-reservation eligibility restrictions, would contradict the described sampling design.
claims.required_inputs: Full eligible lists, cutoffs and historical assignment.

claims.quote: SC population totals are used to rank councils in descending order
claims.years: Rajasthan 1995–2010; Bihar elections discussed in manuscript
claims.procedure: Descending population-total list; reservation rotates across terms.
claims.paraphrase: This version uses counts rather than shares for Rajasthan and Bihar.
claims.qualification: Version-specific account; not an independently verified legal algorithm.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Compare count and share rules against original orders.
claims.contradiction: An eligible GP below the reconstructed SC-population-total cutoff being selected over an otherwise eligible higher-ranked GP would contradict the stated rule, after accounting for rotation, ties and category conflicts.
claims.required_inputs: Historical GP populations, quotas, overlaps and reservation histories.

claims.procedure: Karnataka threshold lotteries; otherwise local as-if-random cutoffs.
claims.paraphrase: Pooled balance yields p = 0.64; authors acknowledge they did not observe the lotteries.
claims.qualification: Balance in selected samples does not demonstrate uniform assignment or no residual geographic heterogeneity.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Evaluate full-pool procedural fit separately from covariate balance.
claims.contradiction: Material reproducible covariate imbalance in the specified samples would contradict the reported balance finding; nonrejection alone neither verifies lotteries nor rules out geographic heterogeneity.
claims.required_inputs: Full assignment lists and lottery records.

claims.procedure: Fix category counts from block populations; select descending group shares, excluding previous reservations.
claims.paraphrase: The account combines population ranking with history-dependent eligibility.
claims.qualification: Reservation histories and category precedence must be reconstructed.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Simple share ranks omit eligibility restrictions.
claims.contradiction: An otherwise eligible lower-share GP receiving reservation while a higher-share eligible GP is omitted would contradict the described ranking, once quota counts, previous reservation and SC/ST precedence are resolved.

claims.quote: chosen at random, by lottery, from this residual pool
claims.procedure: Lottery in the residual eligible pool.
claims.paraphrase: The OBC design rests on conditional lottery assignment.
claims.qualification: The residual pool differs from all GPs.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Test within the reconstructed residual pool.
claims.contradiction: Selection outside the verified residual pool would contradict the stated eligibility rule; calibrated departures from its conditional randomization distribution would count against the lottery account.

claims.quote: One possibility is that some local officials did not follow the rules.
claims.pool: Census villages near the GP-formation threshold
claims.procedure: Population threshold; district first-stage diagnostics.
claims.paraphrase: Weak district first stages motivate noncompliance and staffing hypotheses.
claims.qualification: This is a polity-formation mechanism, not proof of reservation discretion.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Use as a methodological precedent for geographic diagnostics.

claims.procedure: Viability and geographic constraints affect achievable splits.
claims.paraphrase: The appendix considers population viability and contiguity as explanations for deviations.
claims.qualification: These constraints cannot be presumed to explain reservation mismatches.

claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Separate rule exceptions and feasibility from discretionary departures.
claims.contradiction: Demonstrating that every proposed split met the applicable viability and contiguity constraints would rule out those constraints as explanations for the audited departures; this does not identify another cause.

claims.quote: found that the rule held, with no exception

claims.quote: a GP may be reserved for women twice in a row
claims.procedure: List reassignment can change a GP’s rank between elections.
claims.paraphrase: Consecutive women’s reservation can occur under the stated allocation rule.
claims.qualification: Not a claim about Rajasthan or Uttar Pradesh law.

claims.procedure: Independent stratified draws across elections.

claims.pool: Linked GPs in the first observed transition
claims.procedure: Pooled transition test.
claims.paraphrase: The manuscript describes nonrejection as confirmation of independence.
claims.qualification: A non-significant test does not establish independence or rule compliance.

claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.

claims.quote: once a GP is reserved for women, it cannot be reserved again in the subsequent election
claims.years: Study elections; legal effective dates unspecified
claims.procedure: Claimed universal one-cycle exclusion.
claims.paraphrase: The appendix states a categorical no-repeat identification premise.
claims.qualification: Treat as a manuscript claim, not an established legal prescription.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.

claims.quote: Failing to reject independence within a district does not establish random assignment
claims.procedure: Sensitivity analysis using district tests.
claims.paraphrase: The text explicitly limits the interpretation of district nonrejection.
claims.qualification: This caveat should govern the stronger independence wording elsewhere.
claims.evidence_basis: Direct source passage; not independently verified implementation.
claims.cited_origin: Authors’ account in the identified source passage; not independently established by this ledger.
claims.implication: Retain small-sample uncertainty and avoid classifying nonrejection as randomization.
claims.contradiction: No empirical rejection threshold converts nonrejection into proof of random assignment; this methodological qualification does not imply a separately falsifiable assignment algorithm.
claims.required_inputs: Existing district transition summaries.

claims.section: Appendix B: Checking the Implementation of the Reservation Process
claims.procedure: Predict reservation timing from 2001 Census SC population shares and compare with observed histories.
claims.paraphrase: Table B.2 reports 61 of 570 GPs (10.70%) reserved in a different electoral period from that predicted; 21 (3.68%) also have SC shares more than one percentage point from the predicted cutoff. Rates are reported separately for each Samiti.
claims.qualification: The author calls the latter group suspicious misassignments and reports that no survey GP belongs to it (p. 10). He discusses alternative Census inputs, rounding and boundary changes (pp. 6–7, 10). This reconstruction concerns SC reservation, not women’s reservation.
claims.evidence_basis: Online Appendix B, Table B.2 (p. 9), interpretation and survey-sample statement (p. 10); reconstruction inputs and discrepancy definition (pp. 6–7). Counts and percentages visually checked against the table.
claims.cited_origin: Author’s reconstruction using Census 2001, Samiti reservation records, calls to panchayat secretaries and interviews with district electoral officers.
claims.implication: Compare Samiti-level discrepancy rates after matching historical population inputs, reservation histories and cutoffs.
claims.contradiction: A matched reconstruction producing different counts would contradict these reported rates; differences in inputs must first be resolved.
claims.required_inputs: Historical GP boundaries, Census inputs, reservation histories and Samiti allocation cutoffs.
